title: GE OEC One CFD — system identity
summary: What the OEC One CFD is, its regulatory lineage, and its major physical assemblies — Phase 6 representation of capability 1, concepts 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 (existence only), 1.5, 1.6, per Steward's Approve with Constraints verdict.

sourceOfTruth.title: 510(k) Premarket Notification K253269 — OEC One CFD
sourceOfTruth.publisher: U.S. FDA / GE HealthCare (GE Hualun Medical Systems Co., Ltd)

specifications.label: Device type
specifications.value: Mobile C-arm surgical imaging system (Image-Intensified Fluoroscopic X-Ray System, 21 CFR 892.1650, Class II)

specifications.label: Major physical assemblies
specifications.value: Mobile stand with articulating arm; C-shaped apparatus with flat panel detector on one end and X-ray source assembly on the other; 27" 4K touchscreen console

specifications.label: Detector configuration
specifications.value: 21cm and 31cm CMOS flat panel detector options
specifications.note: Existence confirmed. Whether size is a purchase-time configuration or field-swappable is unresolved — Concept 1.3, still Research Pending.

specifications.label: Positioning envelope (axes only, not mechanism)
specifications.value: Lateral rotation, wig/wag, orbital rotation, vertical travel, horizontal travel — specific ranges documented in K253269's predicate comparison table
specifications.note: Deliberately excludes how these axes are actuated — that question belongs entirely to capability 3, still pending device-specific confirmation on manual-vs-power-assisted motion.

specifications.label: Transport power profile
specifications.value: 5-minute standby power for transport between rooms without full restart
specifications.note: M1 source (GE HealthCare product page), not R1 — noted here per the known single-sourceOfTruth-per-block schema limitation rather than split into a second block.

content.fieldNotes: Two items intentionally excluded from this block per Steward's Phase 5 review, not omitted by oversight: PHI/cybersecurity language belongs under capability 8 (Connect and exchange data), which already scopes cybersecurity explicitly — forward-pointer only, no concept duplicated here. The existence of four software configurations previews capability 7's territory and is intentionally left for capability 7 to own once its own open catch-all-overlap question (from Phase 3 item c) resolves — referenced here only as a fact capability 7 must account for, not re-derived.
